# SPE Round r01 Plan: triage agent

Nothing exists yet. This round builds the first triage agent, builds the eval harness, and measures 4 configurations on the 40 historical tickets. I have assumed the 40 tickets and the support lead's labels are available as a file I can copy into the repo. If they are not, step 2 stops and I ask you for them.

## 1. Specify

### Requirement table (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Assign exactly one category from: billing, bug, how-to, account, outage | User: "triage tickets correctly" | Code check: value is in the enum and matches the reference label |
| R2 | Assign exactly one priority from P1 to P4 | User: "triage tickets correctly" | Code check: exact match and within-one match against the reference |
| R3 | Never miss a P1 ticket | Decision (default D3): a missed outage costs more than any other error | Code check: recall on reference P1 tickets |
| R4 | Draft a first reply that addresses the ticket and invents no facts (no refunds, ETAs, or fixes that nobody promised) | Project description: "drafts a first reply" | LLM judge with a fixed rubric. Code cannot check this. |
| R5 | Return output in a fixed JSON schema: category, priority, reply_draft, rationale | Decision: graders need structured output | Code check: JSON schema validation |
| R6 | Keep cost per ticket at or under $0.01 | User: "cheaply". Number is default D2 | Code check: token usage times a pinned price table |
| R7 | Trials see only the ticket text. They never see labels, graders, or predictions | Guidance: trials must not peek | Transcript scan. Any trial that touched those paths is voided. |

There are no proposals from an earlier round. This is round 1.

### Open decisions and defaults (spe/spec/disagreements.md)

| ID | Question | Owner | Default used this round |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What score counts as "correct"? | User | Category accuracy at least 0.85 and priority within-one at least 0.90 |
| D2 | What does "cheaply" mean in dollars? | User | At most $0.01 per ticket, measured on list prices |
| D3 | Is a missed P1 a hard failure? | User | Yes. P1 recall must be 1.0 for a config to pass. |
| D4 | Which model judges the replies? | Claude | An Opus-tier model, so the judge is stronger than every config. Self-preference risk for same-family configs is logged. |
| D5 | Where do few-shot examples come from? | Claude | 5 synthetic tickets that I write. None come from the 40 eval tickets, because that would leak answers. |
| D6 | Which exact model IDs? | Claude | I pin current Haiku-tier and Sonnet-tier IDs from the Claude docs at build time and record them in the plan copy. |
| D7 | Control regrade gate | Claude | No earlier round exists. The control gate grades C0 twice and requires identical scores. |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each config changes one thing from the config before it.

| Config | What it is | Change from previous |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Naive baseline. No model. Always answers the most common category and priority in the labels, with no reply. | Floor |
| C1 | Small model (Haiku tier), zero-shot prompt | Adds a model |
| C2 | Mid model (Sonnet tier), same zero-shot prompt | Model only |
| C3 | Mid model, same prompt plus 5 synthetic few-shot examples | Examples only |

Each config runs each of the 40 tickets 3 times. That makes 120 trials per model config. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

### Prediction table

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid rate | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 0.97 ± 0.03 | 0.99 ± 0.01 | 0.99 ± 0.01 | `checkSchema` | Small models break JSON now and then. Mid models rarely do. |
| Category accuracy | 0.30 ± 0.10 | 0.78 ± 0.07 | 0.85 ± 0.06 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | `checkCategory` exact match | Billing versus account and bug versus outage are the likely confusions. Examples help draw those lines. |
| Priority exact | 0.40 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.08 | 0.62 ± 0.08 | 0.68 ± 0.08 | `checkPriority` exact | Priority follows the support lead's unwritten rules. A prompt alone cannot know them. |
| Priority within one | 0.80 ± 0.10 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.93 ± 0.05 | `checkPriority` within one | Most errors will be off by one level, such as P2 versus P3. |
| P1 recall | 0.00 ± 0.00 | 0.75 ± 0.20 | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.90 ± 0.10 | `checkP1Recall` | Outage words are clear signals. The bands are wide because there are probably only about 4 P1 tickets. |
| Reply pass rate | 0.00 ± 0.00 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.87 ± 0.08 | `judgeReply` rubric (addresses the issue, invents no facts, correct tone) | Small models invent refunds and ETAs more often. Examples barely change reply quality. |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | 0.000 ± 0.000 | 0.003 ± 0.001 | 0.008 ± 0.003 | 0.013 ± 0.004 | `checkCost` usage times pinned prices | The examples add about 1,500 input tokens to each call. |

The naive guess is C0. The close-out will say plainly if C0 beats any model config on any metric.

Expected verdict against the defaults: C2 is the most likely config to pass both D1 and D2. C3 probably fails D2 on cost. All configs probably fail D3, because P1 recall below 1.0 is likely.

## 3. Evaluate

### Steps, with a commit after each

| Step | Work | Gate to continue | Commit message |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Create `spe/` with `README.md`, `spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` (your prompt, verbatim), `spec/spec.md`, `spec/disagreements.md` | Files exist | `spe: scaffold round r01 spec` |
| 1 | Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with the header `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs, bands, a Why per number, and `same_as_last_round: null` | YAML parses | `spe: r01 plan and prediction` |
| 2 | Add `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` (ticket text only) and `spe/evals/answers/labels.jsonl` (reference labels). Trials get no read access to `answers/`. | 40 rows in each file. IDs match. | `spe: add r01 eval data` |
| 3 | Build the agent in `triage/`: system prompt, output schema, few-shot file for C3 | One manual run returns valid JSON | `triage: first agent prompt and schema` |
| 4 | Write `spe/evals/harness/grade.js` with code checks first and the reply judge last | Selftest: oracle labels score 1.0, empty output fails, shuffled labels fail | `spe: r01 grader and selftest` |
| 5 | Write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = "r01"` | Control: C0 graded twice gives identical scores | `spe: r01 workflow script` |
| 6 | Dry run on 3 cells: C1 ticket 1, C2 ticket 5, C3 ticket 12 | All 3 grade end to end. The peek scan runs clean. | `spe: r01 dry run passed` |
| 7 | Launch the Workflow | The launch returns | none until close-out |

### Workflow arguments

- `ROUND`: "r01"
- `configs`: C0, C1, C2, C3
- `tickets`: all 40
- `trials_per_cell`: 3
- `split_cell_extra_trials`: up to 2 more when the 3 trials disagree on category or priority, with a cap of 40 extra trials per config
- `spend_cap_usd`: 15. Any trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged.
- `void_on_peek`: true. The scan covers reads of `spe/evals/answers/`, `spe/evals/harness/grade.js`, and `spe/predictions/`.
- Final stages: failure analysis by category confusion and priority error, then a completeness critic that checks every cell was graded or logged as skipped

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

These figures use list prices that I will check against current docs before launch.

| Item | Calls | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | 120 | $0.32 |
| C2 | 120 | $0.97 |
| C3 | 120 | $1.51 |
| Reply judge | 360 | $4.50 |
| Extra trials on split cells | up to 120 | about $1.00 |
| Total | | about $8.30, capped at $15 |

### Close-out after the completion notice

- `spe/prediction-log.md` gets a row per metric and config with Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under the table, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption.
- `spe/failures.md` gets F-numbered failure types. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure, with original and regraded numbers side by side.
- `spe/spec/spec.md` gets a "Proposed for round r02" table. `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` is written with `status: draft`.
- I update `spe/README.md`, commit, and tag the round locally. I will not push.

### Halt conditions

I halt and report to you if the spend cap is reached, if any trial reads the answer key, if the grader selftest fails, or if D1, D2, or D3 needs your decision before the results can be judged.
critiques: The plan has a requirement table, R1 to R7. It traces each requirement to the prompt ("triage tickets correctly", "cheaply") or to a logged default. Each requirement has a Test column, such as "Code check: recall on reference P1 tickets" and "LLM judge with a fixed rubric."

The prediction table gives every config a number with a band for every metric. Examples are category accuracy "0.78 ± 0.07" for C1 and cost "0.013 ± 0.004" for C3. The table uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every metric row has a Why column, and the Whys explain why the configs differ. One example is "The examples add about 1,500 input tokens to each call." The C0 numbers have no explicit Why. They follow from the stated baseline of "always answers the most common category". The YAML step also promises "a Why per number". This passes, but only just.

Step 1 copies the plan to spe/plans/r01.md and writes spe/predictions/r01.yaml with a do-not-edit header. Step 1 then commits both ("spe: r01 plan and prediction"). The dry run is step 6 and the Workflow launch is step 7, so the commit comes before any trial runs.

Step 7 launches a Workflow with listed arguments. Two gates come before it. Step 4 runs a grader selftest where oracle labels must score 1.0 and empty or shuffled labels must fail. Step 6 is a 3-cell dry run that must grade end to end and pass the peek scan.

The prediction table has a "Grader check" column. It names a specific grader for each metric, such as `checkSchema`, `checkCategory`, `checkPriority` within one, `checkP1Recall`, `judgeReply` with a rubric, and `checkCost`.

The close-out section writes spe/prediction-log.md with Predicted, Measured, and Verdict per metric and config. It also adds a "Which Why broke" section. It seeds the next round with a "Proposed for round r02" table and spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml.
